function: Multi-station collaborative predictive beamforming in ISAC: attention-based GCN maps previous-slot beamforming matrices to next-slot ones, maximizing sum rate under a sensing SNR constraint (pp. 1-4).
system: ISAC vehicular network: M RSUs with ULAs of Nt transmit and Nr receive antennas serve K vehicles, single-station then multi-station phases; 30 GHz; no RIS (pp. 1-4).
method: Attention-based graph convolutional network (graph convolution, self-attention encoder, CNN module, FC layer); unsupervised offline training with a penalty-based sum-rate loss; online prediction (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Own simulation: 2,000-sample dataset of vehicle trajectory snapshots, split 8:1:1; path-loss exponent 2.55, base path loss -70 dB; random initial vehicle positions (p. 4).
test_conditions: 2,000-snapshot dataset split 8:1:1 (training, testing, validation); sweeps of power, antennas (12-20), vehicles (2-12), speed (10, 20 m/s); no unseen condition stated (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Learned: HCL-Net [6] and ECT-Net [7]; single-station system curves (not described as classical); no non-learned baseline (pp. 4-5).
metrics: Average achievable communication sum rate (bits/s/Hz) versus transmit power, vehicles, speed, penalty parameter, epochs; average minimum sensing SNR in dB (pp. 4-5).
complexity: Order of complexity C = O(Ep tau B (K^3 - K^2 + Nt K)); Ep = B = 1 in online prediction (Eq. 16, p. 4).
q1_support: p. 4: "We built a 2,000 sample dataset of continuous vehicle trajectory snapshots"; p. 2: "models signal attenuation over distance". Not met: custom simulator with its own path-loss and steering-vector model; no 3GPP, COST 2100 or DeepMIMO model and no measured data.
q2_support: p. 4: "adapting to varying numbers of RSU antennas and vehicles by adjusting the neural network" and "split into training, testing, and validation sets in an 8 : 1 : 1 ratio". Not met: a scalability claim, not a test; no model trained on one condition is tested on another, and the sweeps of Fig. 3 (p. 5) are not stated to reuse a trained model.
q3_support: p. 4: "comparing our method with two of the most recent and effective predictive beamforming algorithms, HCL-Net [6] and ECT-Net [7]". Not met: both are learned (p. 1: "LSTM-based and Transformer-based predictive beamforming models"); no non-learned method is simulated and the single-station curves of Fig. 3(a) are not described as a classical method.
q4_support: p. 4: "Therefore, the overall complexity can be expressed as" C = O(Ep tau B (K^3 - K^2 + Nt K)), Eq. (16), in the Complexity Analysis, with Ep = B = 1 in online prediction.
q5_support: p. 4: "We built a 2,000 sample dataset of continuous vehicle trajectory snapshots". Not met: a self-generated simulation dataset; the paper gives no code or data link or DOI and uses no public or measured dataset.
notes: Title and DOI on p. 1 match. Area 5: predictive beamforming for ISAC with a communication sum-rate objective and a sensing-SNR constraint (pp. 2-3). q3: HCL-Net [6] and ECT-Net [7] are learned and no non-learned method is simulated; the single-station curves of Fig. 3(a) are not described as a classical method. q2: the scalability claim on p. 4 is not a test in an unseen condition.
